3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: It was an unusual day for the residents of Holsord. Regularly used streets and avenues were blocked off by the military personnel. Many shops and cafes were closed and once crowded stores were now empty. Instead, thousands of residents in Holsord were concentrated in one street, Victory Avenue.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Stretching out through the heart of Holsord, people on both sides of the road were waving their Sordish flags proudly for the military parade.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: I was getting prepared to embark on my trip. It was going to be a short drive down the Victory Avenue until we reached Maroon Palace. My company for this trip was Iosef with Serge, as usual, driving the presidential car.

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: Iosef approached me. He was wearing his decorated ceremony outfit. He carried a sword with a goat head at the handle and his pistol by his hip. He put on his cap.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: Serge appeared from the entrance and joined us.

12.speaker: Iosef Lancea
12.text: “We will depart right after the tank column.”

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: After hearing the loud thump of a book falling down to the floor, he turned to a couple of privates that were doing the preparations on the schedule and started walking in their direction.

16.speaker: Iosef Lancea
16.text: “They will tremble before the Sordish military might.”

18.speaker: Iosef Lancea
18.text: “Private! Can't you do your job properly?”

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: I watched the young soldiers perform a lousy salute to Iosef.

20.speaker: Iosef Lancea
20.text: “WHAT IS THAT SALUTE SOLDIER? WATCH! THIS IS A REAL SALUTE!”

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: He performed an excellent salute and after scolding the privates he walked back.

24.speaker: Player
24.text: “Doesn't give me much confidence that our soldiers do not even know how to properly salute.”

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: Serge performed a salute to Iosef which made Iosef smile under his moustache.

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: We started following Serge through the corridors.

34.speaker: Serge Wolkner
34.text: “Mr. President. Have you seen the tanks? Our planes too?”

35.speaker: Serge Wolkner
35.text: “Rumburg will be so scared when they see this.”

40.speaker: Serge Wolkner
40.text: “My kids were very excited to wake up today. You know. To see the planes fly.”

42.speaker: Iosef Lancea
42.text: “Serge, where did you do your military service?”

43.speaker: Serge Wolkner
43.text: “Morna. 7th Artillery Squadron. I still talk with many of my friends from those days.”

44.speaker: Iosef Lancea
44.text: “The camaraderie of military is never forgotten. I'm still in touch with my friends from basic training as well."

45.speaker: Serge Wolkner
45.text: “What about you, sir? Where did you serve?”

46.speaker: Iosef Lancea
46.text: “All over Sordland. You know, Mr. President was under my command once. Gumren Outpost.”

51.speaker: Player
51.text: “Who can forget about Major Lancea? We called him 'The Relentless'.”

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: Iosef let out a long laugh.

57.speaker: Iosef Lancea
57.text: “I also remember, Mr. President did not like to execute direct orders from his superiors.”

58.speaker: Player
58.text: “I did what needed to be done.”

60.speaker: Player
60.text: “Let's cut the chit chat and do what we are here to do.”

61.speaker: Iosef Lancea
61.text: “Which was disobeying orders. But I won't delve into the past.”

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: We exited the building and walked over to the clearance where the black Kadila, the presidential car, was waiting. It was decorated properly for the event and the top canopy had been removed so that we could stand and wave to people.

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: We entered the car and Serge started the engine. Iosef was standing right next to me.
66.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Military_ExperiencedGenerals"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Military_GreenGenerals"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_A_Parade_IosefWithYou"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Joined_CSP"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Joined_ATO"] == true) == false)

67.speaker: Narrator
67.text: A group of ten, maybe twelve latest technology S-16 fighter jets flew above our heads and I thought that the engine sounds was going to leave me deaf. Loud footsteps of the marching soldiers were followed by loud noises coming from tank engines.

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: We waited for a few minutes for the announcement. Finally, it was our turn. On both sides of the Victory Avenue there were numerous citizens cheering my name, waving their Sordish flags.

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: We kept our slow and steady pace. We were almost at the Artor S. Wisci statue several hundred meters away.
72.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_SollTrial_Guilty_Death"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_SollTrial_Guilty_Prison"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Ending_Coup"] == true) == false)

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: The convoy continued. As I looked around and saw that there was a military truck parked next to the statue in the distance.

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “Hey Iosef, is that truck part of the parade?”

76.speaker: Iosef Lancea
76.text: “Yes it is, sir. Although I am not sure why it is not following the motorcade.”

77.speaker: Iosef Lancea
77.text: “I will make sure they are punished.”

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: We continued and neared the statue.

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: The truck was standing in the middle of the road blocking the parade a few dozen meters in-front of us.

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: His jaw was clenched and his hand was slowly making its way to the gun on his hip.

82.speaker: Player
82.text: “What is going on? Do you see the truck?”

85.speaker: Iosef Lancea
85.text: “What on earth is going on with that truck? Bring the guards at once. Do you copy?”

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: His other hand went to his radio.

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: Three men who jumped out of the truck started running towards our car. They were holding KA-74's pointed right at us.

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: In a split second Iosef pulled his pistol and shot at the gunmen.

91.speaker: Player
91.text: “REVERSE! GET DOWN! THEY ARE GONNA SHOOT!”

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: Serge quickly accelerated the car. The gunmen started firing and my ears started ringing. The sounds of the bullet impacts were horrifying.

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: Serge reversed the car at full speed and ducked.

99.speaker: Iosef Lancea
99.text: “Are you injured? Do you feel any pain?”

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: I checked my body and didn't feel any injuries. I shook my head. I saw the wound on Iosef's right shoulder.

104.speaker: Iosef Lancea
104.text: “It's just a bullet in the shoulder, sir. Nothing critical.”

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: The car horn wouldn't stop blaring. I looked over to the driver's seat.

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: Serge's head was leaning against the wheel, completely motionless.

111.speaker: Iosef Lancea
111.text: “They are dead. I got one of them the guards handled the other two.”

116.speaker: Narrator
116.text: Emergency medical teams arrived and started examining me. After confirming that we had no injuries, I stood up and took a look around.

117.speaker: Narrator
117.text: They started taking care of Iosef and put him on a stretcher. He was yelling.

118.speaker: Iosef Lancea
118.text: <shout>“HOW CAN YOU LET THIS HAPPEN? IDIOTS, ALL OF YOU!”</shout>

119.speaker: Iosef Lancea
119.text: “YOU CAN'T EVEN PROTECT YOUR OWN PRESIDENT! WHY WAS I THE FIRST ONE TO RESPOND?!”

120.speaker: Narrator
120.text: Iosef was put in an ambulance and taken away.

121.speaker: Narrator
121.text: I watched the medics pull out Serge's lifeless body from the car and place it into a black body bag.

122.speaker: Narrator
122.text: Trails of blood were leading to the dead gunmen behind the presidential car.

126.speaker: Narrator
126.text: They started firing and my ears started ringing. I could hear the bullets impacting the car as we reversed and hit a roadblock behind us.

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: I dared to look up for a second and saw that Iosef had his pistol drawn, shooting back at the attackers. I checked my body and didn't feel any injuries.

128.speaker: Narrator
128.text: I saw the wound on Iosef's right shoulder. He was shot.

130.speaker: Player_Italic
130.text: Pull him back to the cover.

131.speaker: Narrator
131.text: As he stumbled, he pointed his pistol, aimed and then fired at the gunmen.

132.speaker: Narrator
132.text: A brief gunfight ensued outside as the police and soldiers rushed over to secure the vehicle. There was a complete silence and the screams from of the crowd subdued.

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: There was a muffled sound from the front seat.

137.speaker: Narrator
137.text: Iosef turned to me after grunting.

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: Iosef turned to me after grunting.

139.speaker: Iosef Lancea
139.text: “I've been better, sir. Got two of them.”

144.speaker: Player
144.text: “No, Serge. I won't be fine until they pay for what they have done.”

148.speaker: Serge Wolkner
148.text: “Mr. Lancea is a tough cookie to crack.”

151.speaker: Narrator
151.text: Emergency medical teams arrived and started examining me. After confirming that we had no injuries, I stood up and took a look around.

152.speaker: Narrator
152.text: They started taking care of Iosef and put him on a stretcher. He was yelling.

153.speaker: Iosef Lancea
153.text: <shout>“HOW CAN YOU LET THIS HAPPEN? IDIOTS, ALL OF YOU!”</shout>

154.speaker: Narrator
154.text: Iosef was put in an ambulance and taken away.

155.speaker: Iosef Lancea
155.text: “YOU CAN'T EVEN PROTECT YOUR OWN PRESIDENT! WHY WAS I THE FIRST ONE TO RESPOND?!”

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: Trails of blood were leading to the dead gunmen behind the presidential car.

157.speaker: Narrator
157.text: I was finally placed in an ambulance as well and was rushed to the hospital.

167.speaker: Narrator
167.text: A couple of old propeller planes flew above our heads and I thought whether the planes were older than me. Loud footsteps of the marching soldiers were followed by loud noises coming from tank engines.

168.speaker: Narrator
168.text: The tanks came into my view. They were top of the line modern battle tanks. Their shining armour under the sun invigorated national pride.

169.speaker: Narrator
169.text: The tanks came into my view. They were not the most modern models however they displayed our military might. I couldn't even finish my thought and one of the tanks broke down and had to be towed.

176.speaker: Narrator
176.text: On the way to the car, generals and admirals were lined up on both sides of the carpet. The atmosphere immediately changed when these experienced men who fought many times for their country saluted me. I saluted back with respect.

177.speaker: Narrator
177.text: On the way to the car, generals and admirals were lined up on both sides of the carpet. I was surprised by the young age of some generals. I wondered whether they have even seen any action.

178.speaker: Narrator
178.text: A group of soldiers saluted me as we passed by. They did not even have matching guns. Iosef turned to me.

179.speaker: Iosef Lancea
179.text: “This is all result of the cuts, Mr. President.”

180.speaker: Narrator
180.text: A group of soldiers saluted me as we passed by. They looked proud and stout in the new infantry uniforms and with brand-new rifles.

181.speaker: Narrator
181.text: We continued on as per the schedule and finally arrived at the Maroon Palace which marked the end of the parade.

182.speaker: Narrator
182.text: People of Holsord dispersed to their homes.

183.speaker: Narrator
183.text: A clear message was sent to Rumburg by the display of our military might.

184.speaker: Narrator
184.text: We were about to see whether it would be enough or not.

193.speaker: Narrator
193.text: We exited the building and walked over to the clearance where the black Kadila, the presidential car, was waiting. It was decorated properly for the event and the top canopy had been removed so that I could stand and wave to people.

197.speaker: Narrator
197.text: I entered the car and Serge started the engine. Iosef saluted me. We were on our way shortly.

201.speaker: Narrator
201.text: Even though there were many walls and trees in between the car and the crowd, I was able to hear the deafening sounds of cheering Sordish citizens. Gradually we made our way to the starting point.

205.speaker: Narrator
205.text: A group of soldiers saluted me as we passed by. They did not even have matching guns.

209.speaker: Narrator
209.text: The convoy continued. As I looked around and saw that there was a military truck parked next to the statue in the distance.

210.speaker: Narrator
210.text: We continued and neared the statue.

211.speaker: Player
211.text: “Hey Serge, is that truck part of the parade?”

213.speaker: Serge Wolkner
213.text: “I think so, Mr. President. Although I am not sure why it's parked.”

214.speaker: Narrator
214.text: The truck was standing in the middle of the road blocking the parade a few dozen meters in-front of us.

217.speaker: Player
217.text: “What is going on? Do you see the truck?”

219.speaker: Narrator
219.text: His jaw was clenched and he was intently watching.

221.speaker: Narrator
221.text: Serge then picked up the radio.

222.speaker: Serge Wolkner
222.text: “There seems to be a truck on the way. Is this part of the schedu-”

223.speaker: Narrator
223.text: Three men who jumped out of the truck started running towards our car. They were holding KA-74's pointed right at us.

226.speaker: Narrator
226.text: Gunmen started firing and my ears started ringing. The sounds of the bullet impacts were horrifying.

227.speaker: Narrator
227.text: There was a complete silence followed by screams from the crowd.

228.speaker: Narrator
228.text: The car hit one of the soldiers. We were about to crash into the truck in-front of us.

229.speaker: Player
229.text: “REVERSE! GET DOWN! THEY ARE GONNA SHOOT!”

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: I regained consciousness after the crash. The muffled screams from the crowd combined with the car horn.

232.speaker: Narrator
232.text: Serge reversed the car at full speed and ducked.

233.speaker: Narrator
233.text: They started firing and my ears started ringing. I could hear the bullets impacting the car as we reversed and hit a roadblock behind us.

236.speaker: Narrator
236.text: There was a muffled sound from the front seat.

240.speaker: Player
240.text: “No, Serge. I won't be fine until they pay for what they have done.”

242.speaker: Narrator
242.text: Emergency medical teams arrived and started examining me and Serge. After confirming that we had no injuries, I stood up and took a look around.

243.speaker: Narrator
243.text: The car was dotted with bullet holes. The bodies of dead gunmen were in-front of it. It was a miracle that no one died.

244.speaker: Narrator
244.text: The car horn just wouldn't stop. I looked over to the driver seat.

245.speaker: Narrator
245.text: Serge's head was leaning against the wheel, completely motionless.

247.speaker: Narrator
247.text: Trails of blood were leading to the dead gunmen behind the presidential car.

248.speaker: Narrator
248.text: Emergency medical teams arrived and started examining me. After confirming that we had no injuries, I stood up and took a look around.

249.speaker: Narrator
249.text: I watched the medics pull out Serge's lifeless body from the car and into a black body bag.

250.speaker: Player_Italic
250.text: Hold on as tightly as you can.

258.speaker: Narrator
258.text: Looking at the benches where the new officers of the General Staff was sitting at, I saw Tarquin Soll.

262.speaker: Narrator
262.text: From this distance it was hard to tell, but he tipped his hat off to me and I could swear that he was smiling.

266.speaker: Narrator
266.text: Looking at the benches where the General Staff was sitting at, I saw Tarquin Soll sitting next to General Valken.

272.text: I saluted the high ranking military staff and attaches from CSP. We shook hands before proceeding.

277.speaker: Narrator
277.text: A brief gunfight ensued outside as the police and soldiers rushed over to secure the vehicle.

278.speaker: Narrator
278.text: A brief gunfight ensued outside as the police and soldiers rushed over to secure the vehicle. My head was spinning and my ears were still ringing.

279.speaker: Narrator
279.text: The car hit one of the soldiers. We were about to crash into the truck in front of us.

282.speaker: Narrator
282.text: A brief gunfight ensued outside as the police and soldiers rushed over to secure the vehicle. Iosef fired several more times towards the gunmen. My head was spinning and my ears were still ringing.

283.speaker: Player_Italic
283.text: Hold on as tightly as you can.

284.speaker: Narrator
284.text: I regained consciousness after the crash. The muffled screams from the crowd combined with the car horn.

286.speaker: Iosef Lancea
286.text: “He served his country until the very end.”
